one_liner: C command-line tool that turns SCAD/CSG models into layered STL for 3D printing, 50-350x faster than OpenSCAD's CGAL render.
what_it_does: Hob3l reads a documented subset of OpenSCAD's SCAD language (or the flattened .csg that `openscad x.scad -o x.csg` writes quickly), plus STL and SVG imports, and writes STL for a slicer, WebGL/JS for previewing, or PostScript and SCAD for debugging. It replaces the `openscad x.csg -o x.stl` render step, not CGAL as a library: the input is a file, the output is a stack of per-layer solids (0.2 mm layers in the README runs), and you still run Slic3r/PrusaSlicer/Cura for toolpaths and G-code. The build also produces static libraries (hob3lbase, hob3lop, hob3lmat, hob3l) with install-lib/install-include targets, but no library API is documented.
how_it_is_fast: It reverses OpenSCAD's 'compute the 3D CSG, then slice' order: each primitive polyhedron is cut into polygons at every layer height first, and the booleans are then done per layer in 2D, which avoids CGAL's Nef-polyhedron 3D booleans entirely. The 2D clipping is a Bentley-Ottmann plane sweep extended with Martinez-Rueda-Feito rules for overlapping edges, evaluating many polygons at once through a boolean function stored as a bit array. Coordinates are 32-bit integers (default unit 1/8192 mm), intersection points use a fixed 160-bit exact fraction instead of a generic bignum library, and de Berg's snap rounding brings results back to input precision before Hertel-Mehlhorn triangulation.
when_to_use: OpenSCAD's F6/CGAL render of a model for FDM printing takes tens of seconds to minutes and you only need a printable STL; the README shows 45.2 s to 0.82 s (x-carriage) and 4m30s to 0.75 s (test31b with $fn=99 ellipsoids)
Models built mainly from unions, differences and intersections of high-facet primitives, where CGAL time grows quickly and Hob3l's per-layer 2D work stays under a second
Edit-and-reload prototyping: write SCAD in an editor, run Hob3l to WebGL/JS (about 0.65 s for the README's curry.scad) and reload a browser viewer
Inputs where CGAL reports 'object may not be a valid 2-manifold' on coincident faces: Hob3l's integer arithmetic and snap rounding are built to produce valid 2-manifold output there
when_not_to_use: You need a single exact 3D solid (for CAD export, FEM, machining or further mesh booleans): output is separate stacked layers with visible stair-stepping, and Slic3r's split makes it many objects

Models that rely on 3D hull(), minkowski(), offset(), resize() or render(): hull() is 2D only, projection() supports cut=true only, and SCAD variables, functions and modules must first be flattened by OpenSCAD's .csg export
Long-running or embedded use: the author says memory leaks are not fixed because the tool starts, allocates and exits
macOS: issue #11 (open, 'help wanted') reports a segfault slicing a .scad file there; development and testing are on Linux, with MinGW cross builds
Comparing against current OpenSCAD: the timings are against its CGAL render path from the 2018 era, not OpenSCAD's newer Manifold backend

integration.form: CLI executable (hob3l) plus static libraries (hob3lbase, hob3lop, hob3lmat, hob3l) with installable headers; no documented library API
integration.dependencies: none beyond a C compiler, libc/POSIX, GNU make and Perl (Perl scripts generate C code at build time); OpenSCAD is optional as a .scad-to-.csg preprocessor
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (-std=c11) with GCC extensions (statement expressions, __typeof__); GCC or Clang, MinGW for Windows cross builds
integration.platforms: Linux (development platform); Windows via MinGW cross-compile (win32/win64 targets); 32- and 64-bit x86 gcc targets; macOS has an open segfault report (#11)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces the `openscad model.csg -o model.stl` CGAL render step for printing, but reads only a SCAD subset and produces layered rather than solid 3D output

gotchas: $fa and $fs are accepted but ignored (only $fn is used), so circle and sphere faceting can differ from OpenSCAD's output
Stricter parser than OpenSCAD: arguments the OpenSCAD docs call mandatory are rejected when missing, where OpenSCAD silently defaults them
The default build (MODE=normal) is -O2 with runtime checks on (NDEBUG off); MODE=release gives -O3 and -DNDEBUG. The README's '-march=native' default actually applies only in MODE=devel
Input polyhedra with holes (missing faces) are not supported (README). Separately, users hit the assertion 'Odd number of edges meet in one point' (issues #5 and #9, both closed)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Hob3l over Manifold, MeshLib or kigumi only when the goal is a printable layered STL from SCAD and you never need the exact 3D boolean result; those siblings compute real mesh booleans (Manifold is also what newer OpenSCAD builds can use instead of CGAL) and are the choice when the solid itself matters.
verified_claims_summary: First-party `time` wall-clock runs from the README: OpenSCAD's CGAL 3D CSG render vs Hob3l at 0.2 mm layers on two Prusa i3 MK3 parts and two of the author's own models (45.2 s vs 0.82 s, 2m42s vs 1.24 s, 53.4 s vs 0.61 s including a 23 MB STL write, and 4m30s vs 0.75 s). No CPU, compiler, flags or OpenSCAD version is stated, the outputs differ in kind (layered vs solid), and per GitHub's blame view the timings date from October 2018, before the April 2023 'replace core by robust integer arithmetics' rewrite.
status_note: Stale single-author hobby project (last commit 2024-06-23, 341 commits, no releases shown, 4 open issues) under GPL-3.0, so linking it into proprietary code is not an option, though the standalone CLI is easy to build with no third-party libraries.
